title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes-lee
body:
Notes / breadcrumbs for SSE/chunking/backpressure bug (personal scratchpad)

Context:
- Observed intermittent client hangs / partial streams from hosted API when load spikes. Mostly affects SSE and chunked responses (chat streaming).
- Affects both NodeJS and Python clients. Appears more likely when upstream model response has bursts of tokens separated by >50ms gaps.
- Environment: local repro with nginx reverse-proxy -> envoy -> runtime (go) in k8s; also saw on Dedicated with ALB.

Symptoms observed:
- Client receives initial headers and first few events, then stops getting further chunks for long time (client still connected).
- On server side, write() calls succeed (no errors), but bytes not being flushed immediately.
- nginx logs show 200 and connection kept-open; sometimes shows proxy_buffering on.
- Envoy stats: downstream_rq_pending_active increases; upstream downstream flushes delayed.
- Errors seen in logs: "write EPIPE" only in one case where client disconnected; common messages: none obvious.
- Repro run with wrk: throughput drops significantly when many concurrent streaming connections.

Hypotheses:
- Proxy buffering (nginx proxy_buffering / proxy_request_buffering) is coalescing chunks and only forwarding when buffer fills or connection closes.
- Envoy HTTP connection pool + upstream flow control: envoy may buffer small writes and apply backpressure incorrectly when upstream pauses between small writes.
- Kernel TCP write coalescing and Nagle interacting with application-level flush semantics.
- Application not setting correct headers for SSE (Content-Type: text/event-stream; Cache-Control: no-transform) so intermediate proxies transform or buffer.
- Chunked encoding mis-signalling (content-length header present erroneously) causing proxies to wait for end of stream.

Repro steps I used locally (minimal):
1) Simple SSE server (node) that emits "data: <i>\n\n" every ~75ms. Run behind nginx + envoy config.
   - Node example (for local quick test):
     const http = require('http');
     http.createServer((req, res) => {
       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-transform', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no' });
       let i = 0;
       const t = setInterval(() => { res.write(`data: ${i}\n\n`); i++; if (i>50) { clearInterval(t); res.end(); } }, 75);
     }).listen(8081);

2) curl to nginx endpoint: curl -N localhost:8080/sse-test -v
   - curl shows first ~5 events reliably, then pauses for ~10-30s, sometimes resumes.

3) curl with --no-buffer and --no-keepalive: curl --no-buffer --raw --header "Accept: text/event-stream" http://localhost:8080/sse-test
   - Slightly better but still sees pauses.

4) Python requests streaming test:
   import requests
   r = requests.get(url, stream=True)
   for line in r.iter_lines():
     if line: print(line)

   - Same pause behavior.

5) Reproduced with a direct request to runtime (bypass nginx/envoy): curl -N localhost:8081/sse-test
   - Direct to Node server: smooth, no pauses. => strongly suggests proxy layer interaction.

Things tried so far (commands & config changes):
- nginx.conf:
  location /sse-test {
    proxy_pass http://upstream;
    proxy_buffering off;  # tried enabling/disabling
    proxy_request_buffering off;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    chunked_transfer_encoding on;
    proxy_set_header Connection "";
    # X-Accel-Buffering: no header from app also tested
  }
  Result: proxy_buffering off + X-Accel-Buffering: no improved in some runs but not consistently.

- Envoy config tuning:
  - increased upstream/outbound_buffer limits and lowered max_request_bytes
  - toggled use of http/1.1 vs http/2 between nginx <-> envoy
  Result: some improvement when forcing nginx->envoy to use HTTP/1.1 (less framing surprises), but still intermittent.

- Application-level flushes:
  - In Go runtime, explicitly call w.(http.Flusher).Flush() after each Write() for streaming code paths. Verified flusher present.
  Result: Required and good practice; didn't completely eliminate pauses (but reduced frequency).

- Headers:
  - Ensure Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
  - Add Cache-Control: no-transform, Connection: keep-alive, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, X-Accel-Buffering: no
  Result: needed; some proxies ignored unless both Cache-Control and X-Accel-Buffering present.

- Kernel / TCP tweaks on test hosts (nagle off via TCP_NODELAY):
  - Set TCP_NODELAY at socket level in app. Minor improvement.

- repro with wrk: wrk -t12 -c200 -d30s -- script that reads body and doesn't close
  Observed proxy memory and buffer growth then stalls.

Interesting logs/snippets:
- nginx error_log (debug):
  [debug] proxy: sending body chunk, len=14
  [debug] proxy: buffered 16384 bytes, waiting to send

- Envoy admin /stats:
  upstream_flow_control_queued_buffered_bytes > 0 during pause periods
  downstream_cx_active spikes then stablizes

- Sample runtime trace (Go):
  Write into response writer: wrote 14 bytes
  Flush invoked
  syscall.Write returned 14
  but downstream bytes_sent in envoy stays same until buffer threshold

Next steps / TODOs:
- Make a minimal docker-compose repro: nginx -> envoy -> simple go/node server that emits tokens with configurable pause. Share compose + config. (Start this)
- Re-run with nginx debug logs + envoy debug logging during repro and capture pcap to inspect TCP-level flow.
- Try disabling nginx entirely (nginx->envoy in front) to confirm where buffering occurs (already did direct->app, so suspect nginx/envoy interplay).
- Try proxying with haproxy directly (bypass envoy), see if HAProxy buffers.
- Add instrumentation to runtime to log when Flush actually reaches network (tcp bytes acked) vs when write syscall returns.
- Reproduce with ALB setup (Dedicated) to see parity with cloud infra; ALB has known buffering quirks for chunked responses.

Quick mitigation ideas for customers:
- For SSE routes, recommend "proxy_buffering off" (nginx), X-Accel-Buffering: no from app, and ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked and no Content-Length headers.
- Force nginx->envoy to use HTTP/1.1 where possible; HTTP/2 can add headers/stream multiplexing complexity that causes buffering/delay under certain envoy configs.
- Tune envoy buffer limits or use flush-on-write behaviour if available in envoy config (upstream_flush_on_write?).
- Implement client-side keep-alive/heartbeat to detect stalls and reconnect gracefully.

Notes to self:
- This is messy because multiple layers can buffer; reproduce with the minimal chain and then incrementally add proxies.
- Get infra team to run binary search on which proxy is the main offender (nginx vs envoy vs ALB).
- Write up playbook after we get deterministic repro.

Commands to reproduce quickly (local):
1) start simple sse server (node) on :8081 (paste server code above)
2) nginx config (minimal) with proxy_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, location /sse-test -> upstream 127.0.0.1:8081
3) curl -N localhost:8080/sse-test -v  (observe stalls)
4) curl directly to 8081 (no stalls)
5) tcpdump -i lo -s 0 -w sse-repro.pcap port 8080 or 8081 while reproducing

Misc references I used recently:
- https://www.nginx.com/resources/wiki/start/topics/examples/streaming/
- Envoy docs on HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 bridging and flow control
- Thread: "SSE/Chunked responses being buffered by nginx" on stackoverflow (useful hints about proxy_buffering and X-Accel-Buffering)

If I get a deterministic repro, next step is to open GH issue in serving-runtime and link to this doc + add small test harness.

Other random observations:
- When I increased server chunk size ~> 1KB per write (instead of ~10-30 bytes), behavior improved significantly. That suggests either Nagle or proxy buffer thresholds are at play.
- On the cloud Dedicated instance (ALB), ALB appears to buffer until ~16KB chunks; small tokenized writes were coalesced causing perceived stutter.

End of notes.

-- Lee
